questions.q: The final model scored ROC AUC 0.807 on the test set, versus 0.776 in cross-validation. What is the right way to handle this?
options: Report the test number and avoid going back to adjust the model to push it higher
Retrain until the test score reaches 0.85
Discard the cross-validation result
Add the test rows to the training set and report the new score as the test result
questions.explain: With only 400 test rows some variation is expected. Adjusting the model after seeing the test score would make the estimate optimistic.

questions.q: In the confusion matrix [[229, 33], [70, 68]], what does the 70 represent?
options: Customers who stayed and were correctly cleared
Customers who churned but were missed by the model
Customers wrongly flagged as churners
Customers correctly caught as churners
questions.explain: Rows are actual and columns are predicted, so the bottom-left cell is churners predicted to stay: the false negatives.

questions.q: Lowering the threshold from 0.5 to 0.3 changed recall from 0.493 to 0.812 and precision from 0.673 to 0.557. Which statement is correct?
options: The model became strictly better
The model catches more churners but flags more customers who would have stayed, so the choice depends on the cost of outreach versus the cost of losing a customer
Precision and recall always move in the same direction
The threshold has no effect on the outreach list size
questions.explain: A lower threshold trades precision for recall. The list of flagged customers grew from 101 to 201, so the business must weigh that cost.

questions.q: The silhouette scores for k = 2 to 6 were between about 0.25 and 0.29. How should you treat the k-means segments?
options: As definitive natural groups
As invalid because silhouette must be above 0.9
As a useful descriptive lens, not truth, since there are no sharply separated groups
As proof that k must equal 2
questions.explain: Low, flat silhouettes mean the structure is weak. Choosing k = 3 was for interpretability, and the segments describe patterns rather than natural categories.

questions.q: Which is the best way to open a portfolio presentation for a business audience?
options: A walkthrough of every hyperparameter you tried
The mathematics of logistic regression
A list of libraries used
The decision the audience needs to make and your recommendation, then the supporting evidence
questions.explain: Lead with the business decision and recommendation, then show how the analysis supports it and be candid about the limitations.
